properties.name: The handshake record names the revision rmcp actually sent: reflow2's copy of rmcp's negotiation rule is rmcp 3.5.0's, and a wire test compares the two
properties.rationale: Root cause: fact:root-cause-the-handshake-record-named-a-revision-rmcp-never-sent-2026-10-02. The class is a rule maintained by hand with a test that compared the copy with itself; the same class as the latent tool list (fact:root-cause-the-latent-tool-list-omits-the-cache-fields-the-2026-07-28-spec-requires-2026-09-26). corrected_cause because the new test compares the copy with rmcp's behaviour rather than with itself, so any future divergence fails it. The wire answer was always right: rmcp re-runs its own rule on what the override returns.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: handshake::negotiate, the copy of rmcp's pub(crate) negotiate_protocol_version, was copied at 3.1.2 and drifted at 3.4.0: rmcp echoes only a version that has a handshake and replaces a fallback without one by the newest supported one that does. The copy is now rmcp 3.5.0's rule (None = rmcp's unsupported_protocol_version refusal, returned by the initialize override). tests/an_initialize_is_recorded_as_rmcp_answered_it.rs compares <graph>.client.json's `negotiated` with the version on the wire, over the real binary, for every revision rmcp knows plus 2024-01-01 and 2027-01-01 — observed failing against the pre-fix rule (record 2026-07-28, wire 2025-11-25) and passing after.
